- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.3) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.3), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes — especially if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative — leading to overcorrection; dampen peak forecasts.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is significantly above recent 5-10 day average, reduce by 5-10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum — especially after strong sentiment shifts — so add a 1-2 day lag correction to align with true outcome’s tail.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.3 → -0.3 → +0.3), model tends to misread trend direction; apply smoothing filter to sentiment-weighted average before forecasting.
